answer: In a reputation system, each agent identity accrues trust slowly through verified transactions over months, building a beacon of reliability. New identities start at zero, forcing attackers to either wait or operate in a low-trust nebula where rates are poor and partners scarce. Dormant accounts decay automatically, their signal fading week by week. An attacker spawning a thousand identities gains nothing without the time-cost to age them all, making sybil floods economically futile.
